title: Multiplatform Testing
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of multiplatform testing using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates multiplatform testing.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Multiplatform Testing** as part of **Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform**. Reliable Kotlin code is supported by repeatable tests, meaningful assertions, debuggable failure reports, documentation, and review—not by coverage alone. Use the subtopics—Common Tests, Platform-Specific Tests, CI Builds Across Targets—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Multiplatform work succeeds when shared code depends only on common APIs and platform-specific code is isolated behind deliberate interfaces.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Reliable Kotlin code is supported by repeatable tests, meaningful assertions, debuggable failure reports, documentation, and review—not by coverage alone.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with common tests. Then compare it with platform-specific tests. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Common Tests
items.text: Common Tests helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.

items.title: Platform-Specific Tests
items.text: Platform-Specific Tests helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.

items.title: CI Builds Across Targets
items.text: CI Builds Across Targets is part of reproducible project configuration. Declare the dependency or plugin where it belongs, preserve a compatible version set, and use the Gradle Wrapper for repeatable builds.

content_blocks.expected_output: Test passes: expected 7 equals actual 7 (requires a Kotlin test runner).
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run inside a Kotlin Multiplatform project with the target toolchains installed; common and platform-specific source sets have different APIs.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Multiplatform Testing removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.

items.title: Explain
items.text: Describe the main rule of multiplatform testing in your own words.

items.title: Apply
items.text: Change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

items.title: Verify
items.text: Check one edge case and the official reference for the selected Kotlin/runtime version.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small variation that demonstrates multiplatform testing. Write down your predicted result first, run it in the correct local project, then explain one boundary case involving common tests.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain multiplatform testing without copying the lesson wording.
Demonstrate the concept with a small code/configuration change and state the expected result.
Test one boundary case or explain a relevant platform/version limitation.
hints: Begin with the first syllabus subtopic: Common Tests. What input or state does it act on?
Change only one value, branch, declaration, or dependency at a time. Predict what should happen before running the code.
